summary: Iter 21 BACKEND-ONLY verification of three P3 security-hardening fixes on Women's Health + Community endpoints. Result: 22/22 tests PASS (100%; one skipped as designed, one transient ConnectTimeout in the initial run that passed cleanly on retry). Fix 1 (community like 404): POST /api/community/posts/{post_id}/like returns 404 'Post not found' for both a made-up id ('nonexistent-uuid-1234') and a random uuid.uuid4(); creating+deleting a post then liking it also returns 404 (verified — no more silent success, no orphan like row). Valid like/unlike toggle by another user still increments/decrements like_count correctly and liked_by_me flips as expected. Fix 2 (race-safe like counter): confirmed the unique compound index 'uniq_post_user_like' on community_likes(post_id, user_id) with unique=True exists (fetched directly from Mongo via motor). Firing 6 concurrent POST /like from a single user against the same post leaves like_count in {0,1} (never 2..6). Toggle sequence off→on→off→on→off ends with like_count == 0 exactly (never negative, never >0). Fix 3 (rate limits): POST /api/women/period-log — 20/hour/user: 21st call returns 429 with first 20 all 200 (verified). PUT /api/women/pregnancy — 30/hour/user: 31st call returns 429 (verified — passed on retry after transient ingress timeout in first run). PUT /api/women/gynae-profile — 30/hour/user: 31st returns 429 (verified on retry). POST /api/family/members/{id}/milestones/toggle — 120/hour/user: 10 successive toggles all return 200 (verified not rate-limited under normal use). GET /api/women/wellness-tips?phase=follicular — 60/5min/IP: 429 reached within 61 quick GETs. Regression: women's health CRUD works (period-log create/list/delete round-trip with correct next_period_predicted = '2026-01-10'+30d = '2026-02-09' and fertile_window populated; pregnancy set with lmp='2026-04-01' returns due_date='2027-01-06' (+280d) and 10 milestones; gynae upsert/get round-trips pcos/pcod/conditions/surgeries/medications/notes). Community post create+list+get+delete+comments intact. Milestones cross-user access still returns 404. Prior findings SEC-001 (5 common default passwords rejected AND ADMIN_PASSWORD from /app/backend/.env logs in as is_admin=true, role=admin), SEC-002 (/support/chat 11th call returns 429 within 12 quick calls), SEC-003 (patient booked appt then attempted POST /prescription -> 403 'Only the treating doctor...') all still resolved. Admin credentials loaded from /app/memory/test_credentials.md via backend/.env ADMIN_PASSWORD. Backend was restarted once at start to reset in-memory rate-limit buckets to a deterministic state.
action_items: None required for iter-21 security-hardening scope. All three P3 fixes verified working. Optional pre-existing recommendations from iter-20 (dedupe hashtags, bounded liked_by_me lookup, distinguish 'never set' vs 'is_active=true but lmp missing' in GET /women/pregnancy, split server.py into domain modules) still stand but are non-blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix 1 implementation (server.py:3603-3606) does a find_one({id:post_id}, {_id:1}) projection before touching the likes collection — cheap and correct.

Fix 2 uses insert_one wrapped in try/except (server.py:3615-3619). Under a duplicate-key race the DuplicateKeyError is swallowed and the $inc is skipped, so like_count is not double-incremented. Note the current handler catches bare Exception; consider narrowing to pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError so genuine Mongo failures (e.g. connection drop) don't silently succeed. Also observed under concurrent tap testing: the current guard successfully kept the final counter in {0,1} across 6 concurrent toggles.
server.py:3611 correctly conditions the $inc:-1 on res.deleted_count > 0, preventing negative counts on a concurrent double-unlike.

rate_limit() (server.py:112-128) uses in-memory _rate_buckets keyed by '{key}:{ip}'. Two implications: (a) buckets reset on backend restart — good for testability; (b) in a multi-replica deploy each pod has its own bucket, so the effective limit is N_replicas × configured limit. Consider Redis-backed rate limiting before scaling out (not blocking for iter-21).

server.py:3477 wellness_tips uses `request: Request = None` default. Works, but a Query-only default of None on a Request param is unusual FastAPI; consider making it a positional required Request param (like the other handlers). Currently the guard `if request is not None` protects the call.
server.py:3306 toggle_milestone applies rate_limit AFTER the member lookup would be fair — order is currently rate_limit first, then find_one. Order is fine (limit protects DB), just noting.
General: server.py is now 3704 lines. Splitting /women, /community, /family into separate routers/modules would materially improve maintainability. This is legacy debt carried since iter-19.

success_rate.backend: 100% (22/22 after retrying one transient network timeout; core assertions all pass)

seed_data_creation: Registered ~10 ephemeral TEST_ users (email prefix test_iter21_*@vaidhyaji.example.com): 2 module-scoped patients (patient_a, patient_b) + 8 short-lived users for the rate-limit and regression tests. Inserted ~6 community_posts (all with content prefixed 'TEST_iter21 ...'; those under Fix 1/Fix 2 tests are deleted by the tests themselves — one intentional survivor from TestRegressionCommunity is also deleted at test end). Inserted 1 community_comment. Inserted ~7 community_likes rows (all removed by the tests via toggle-off). Created 2 family_members docs (TEST_iter21_kid, TEST_iter21_kidB) and 1 appointment (TEST_iter21 checkup) which are left in place; these will be swept if E1 has a nightly cleanup, otherwise they're harmless. Wrote ~20 women_cycles + ~30 women_pregnancy + ~30 women_gynae docs across the rate-limit tests (each keyed to a unique ephemeral user_id). Backend restarted once before test run to clear in-memory rate-limit buckets.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All three P3 security-hardening fixes are verified in /app/backend/tests/test_iter21_security_hardening.py — reuse it as regression harness. Key gotcha: the wellness-tips rate limit (60/5min per IP) is per-IP and shared across ALL test runs from the same public IP, so the last-scheduled test in TestRegressionWomensHealth.test_wellness_tips_for_all_6_phases will skip (not fail) if the rate-limit test above already exhausted the bucket. This is by design. Rate limits are in-memory (see rate_limit at server.py:112), so restarting the backend (`sudo supervisorctl restart backend`) resets all buckets deterministically before a fresh run. Unique index 'uniq_post_user_like' on community_likes(post_id, user_id) is created idempotently on startup (server.py:1631-1636); the log line 'Could not create community_likes unique index' would indicate a create-index failure worth investigating. For SEC-003, the test books an appointment against the first doctor returned by GET /api/doctors — if the seeded doctors change, the test still works since it just picks doctors[0].
rca_of_issue: One test (test_gynae_profile_30_per_hour_31st_returns_429) failed on the initial pytest run with a urllib3 ConnectTimeoutError to the preview ingress after ~14 requests. Isolated re-run of the same test completed in 3.64s and passed cleanly. Root cause: transient ingress connect timeout unrelated to the fix under test — likely momentary preview-tunnel congestion. Not a defect in the rate-limit implementation. No mitigation needed in server code; if flakiness recurs consider adding a urllib3 Retry adapter to the test session or bumping per-request timeout above 15s.
